details.publicNotes:
Eunidois are sadistic killers whose bodies are revolting facsimiles of the titanic cave worms that prowl far underground. Simple eyes adorn their segmented bodies, flickering rapidly with paranoia, while their heads sport three bony mandibles coated in fine bristles. These bristles help them optimize the positioning of their mandibles to cause their prey as much pain as possible. Eunidoi's mouths are shallow caverns containing a forest of spine-covered tongues dripping with toxic mucus. Yet these caverns lead nowhere, as eunidois lack a stomach. Instead, they feed on their prey's suffering and terror.

Most eunidois prefer to lounge around in burrowed tunnel networks and lie in wait for others to approach, whereupon they pounce and rapidly drag their prey to a secluded area. As such, these qlippoths are often found near places of great contention: borders between qlippoth and demon realms, interplanar portals, and other well-trodden paths. Though their habits could have made them helpful guardians for other qlippoths, they avoid making alliances as a matter of course. Eunidoi are fundamentally incapable of understanding the concept of trustworthiness. They only work with other creatures if they are certain they can temporarily exploit and kill them once their usefulness has expired.

More And Less Than Worms

Though they bear a superficial resemblance to cave worms—and indeed, often share territory with such creatures—eunidois are both more cunning and far less physically imposing. Eunidois are generally uninterested in preying upon their larger neighbors and are smart enough to avoid them, even while using their tunnels to track down prey that the cave worms might have missed. If cornered by a cave worm, however, a eunidoi might call out to nearby adventurers for help, offering information in exchange for help defeating the more powerful predator.

You force the target to see a vision of its own death. It takes 8d6 mental damage with a Will save. If the target is reduced to 0 HP by this spell, its vision becomes reality and kills it instantly.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as it's frightened.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

Illusory pain wracks the target, dealing 2d4 mental damage and @Damage[(@item.level)d4[persistent,mental]] damage. The target must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes full initial damage but no persistent damage, and the spell ends immediately.

Failure The target takes full initial and persistent damage, and the target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. If the target recovers from being Sickened, the persistent damage ends and the spell ends.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d4 and the persistent damage by 1d4.

You instantly transport yourself and any items you're wearing and holding from your current space to an unoccupied space within range you can see. If this would bring another creature with you—even if you're carrying it in an extradimensional container—the spell is lost.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 1 mile. You don't need to be able to see your destination, as long as you have been there in the past and know its relative location and distance from you. You are then temporarily immune for 1 hour.

You cause the target to see all other creatures as dire threats. The target is stricken by intense paranoia toward all creatures around it and must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target believes everyone it sees is a potential threat. It becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.I1ffBVISxLr2gC4u]{Unfriendly} to all creatures to which it wasn't already hostile, even those that were previously allies. It treats no one as an ally. The spell ends after 1 round.

Failure As success, but the effect lasts 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, except the target believes that everyone it sees is a mortal enemy. It uses its reactions and free actions against everyone, regardless of whether they were previously its allies, as determined by the GM. It otherwise acts as rationally as it normally does and likely prefers to attack creatures that are actively attacking or hindering it over those leaving it alone.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 5 creatures.

You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.equipment.Item.bikFUFRLwfdvX2x2]{Invisibility Potion}) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

The eunidoi recovers from the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, slowed, and stunned conditions at the end of its turn. It's also immune to penalties to its Speeds and the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} condition, and it ignores difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain.

As Improved Grab, but the eunidoi's Improved Grab does not end when it moves. Instead, it carries the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} creature with it.

A eunidoi can burrow through solid stone at a Speed of 15 feet. It can leave a tunnel if it desires, and it usually does.

The eunidoi's mandibles snap open, revealing a gaping mouth filled with bristled tongues. Creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28] save, after which they are temporarily immune to further Frightening Displays for 1 minute.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and can't reduce the value of its frightened condition below 1 for 1 minute.

Frequency Once per round

Effect The eunidoi Strides or Burrows and then Strikes. If the eunidoi began this action hidden, it remains hidden until after the Strike.
